borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
description:
Subdivision of
commercial units to form 4no. self-contained commercial units within ground
floor rear outbuildings.
decision_conditions: The proposed commercial intensification would not be suitable for this location. It would present as back-land development and create a secondary retail frontage which has no distinct street presence. It would not be suitable for the Neighbourhood Centre location and result in some harm to the character and distinctiveness of the Dagenham Village Conservation Area. Officers therefore consider the proposed development and its use would appear out of the area's character and would negatively impact the viability of the Mark's Gate Neighbourhood Centre, which is contrary to the following planning policies: National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (December, 2024)Policies SD6, SD7 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policy DME3 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September, 2024)

The proposed development would result in harm to the character of the Dagenham Village Conservation Area. The proposal would detract from the built form and historic setting of the area and would fail to preserve the characteristic which the Conservation Area Character Appraisal intends to preserve and protect. Officers consider the harm to arise to the conservation area to be contrary to the following policies which guide proposals to protect and preserve the historic environment:National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (December, 2024)Policy HC1 of the London Plan (March 2021) Policies SP2, DMD1 and DMD4 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September, 2024)

In the absence of sufficient information, officers are unable to determine whether the proposed development would have an acceptable impact to the highway network or whether additional parking could be accommodated for visitors. It also fails to demonstrate how deliveries and servicing will take place. There is an overall lack of evidence to show that it would not cause harm to highway safety. The proposal fails to comply with the following policies which seek to ensure that proposals mitigate impacts to transport networks:National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (December 2024)Policy T6.3 of the London Plan (March 2021)
